additional_explicit_obligations.obligation: Expand imported DIGIT and HEXDIG and audit the used ABNF composition/operator semantics against pinned RFC5234.
Bind the complete applicable RFC3629 UTF-8 validity rules, including overlongs, surrogate values, maximum scalar and truncation behavior.
Apply RFC2119/RFC8174 force and record deliberate SHOULD uniqueness exceptions without upgrading SHOULD/MAY to MUST.
Select Unicode authority/version applicability and verify the ECMA-404 syntax-alignment reference; distinguish code units, code points, scalars and noncharacters.
Record IEEE754 as conditional interoperability guidance for this lexeme-preserving API; do not fabricate a required JSON arithmetic library.
For any claimed transport, bind application/json and published parameter/charset policy to actual MIME/HTTP behavior; no such transport operation is supplied here.
Check IETF Trust document and extracted-code conditions for the exact redistributed material.
Define actual limit metrics and maintain distinct resource-refusal versus invalid-syntax classifications, including the depth and node/lexeme issues in F01/F02.

whole_document_section_review.review_rationale: Describes language-independent data interchange and Standards Track publication. Publication status is not certification of this implementation; no runtime rule is added here.
RFC text and extracted code components have IETF Trust legal conditions. Distribution review is separate from whether implementing JSON grammar requires a proprietary runtime license.
Type/data-model definitions and Unicode citation are represented by P01 and dependency work. Historical JavaScript derivation does not import execution semantics.
BCP14 applies only to uppercase keywords, and ABNF is delegated to RFC5234. The keyword-definition list is metalinguistic and is not ten extra feature obligations.
Authority replacement, special ECMA alignment and future coordination are covered. Coordination duties belong to the standards organizations rather than a parser API.
Historical errata motivate the revision; they are not new independent runtime features to import on top of the published revised grammar.
All eight local productions in this section and the four allowed whitespace terminals are represented. The one-value top-level rule includes scalars.
All four local productions and two operative MUST statements are represented; no other literal names are allowed in the JSON grammar.
Object/member grammar, SHOULD uniqueness and receiver/order caveats are represented. Duplicate acceptance and local lossless behavior remain distinct.
Array grammar, order and heterogeneous values are represented.
All ten numeric productions are represented. Number syntax, permitted limits and conditional binary64 interoperability need separate treatment.
All five string productions and mandatory escaping are represented; imported HEXDIG and Unicode/UTF16 interpretation remain dependency obligations.
Open-interchange UTF-8, network no-BOM and optional input-BOM handling are represented. Closed ecosystems are outside this selected transport profile.
Unpaired-surrogate syntax and interoperability warnings are represented. Accepting an escape is not a promise that arbitrary receivers agree on it.
Decoded code-unit equality guidance is represented. The standard does not supply a general Unicode normalization/collation API.
Parser acceptance, optional extensions and each named permitted-limit class are represented; actual metric semantics require the qualifications identified in this review.
Every generated output must conform. The caller IR domain is an implementation contract; the RFC does not require generating every possible text.

Registration has application/json, no defined parameters, binary encoding, .json and the published charset note. This is a transport-registration boundary, not an HTTP implementation supplied by the parser.
Eval security guidance and U+2028/U+2029 distinction are covered. Modern ECMAScript behavior is version-dependent and is not used as the JSON acceptance oracle.
Both composite examples and all three scalar examples are represented as finite acceptance inputs, not as a conformance proof.
All seven normative references identified; the source-body review is complete but the normative-reference closure is not.
Historical RFCs, ECMAScript and prior errata are informative, so they do not silently extend the selected JSON syntax or runtime contract.
Changes explain authority, UTF-8 and security revisions; each operational change is already reflected in the main-body obligations.
Attribution/contact information adds no implementation feature obligations.
